text:
sophie: Quick sync — I'm prototyping a new Console view that surfaces per-route quota 'burn rate' (tokens/sec) and an estimated time-to-soft-cap. We need to align SDK/client behavior so the numbers in Console are meaningful.

raj: Nice. What's driving the mismatch today?

sophie: Two things: (1) clients doing aggressive client-side batching hide instant spike patterns; (2) sampled telemetry sometimes drops short-lived high-throughput routes so burn rate underestimates.

kelly: For (1) can we expose both server-side token counts and a 'client-batched' counter? Might confuse UX though.

amanda: We could add a column: "observed tokens (server)" vs "tokens attributed (client)". Console can default to server counts, and devs can toggle attribution mode.

tom: From SDK side — Go and Python currently aggregate requests in the background. If we change the batching window, that will instantly shift burn rate. We should avoid surprises for customers.

chris: Agreed. Proposal: SDKs emit an optional header when batching is enabled (opt-in): `X-RW-Client-Batch: true` and `X-RW-Batch-Window-ms: 50`. Console / backend can use that to reconstruct an adjusted burn rate.

raj: How do we handle telemetry sampling? If the backend samples 1% of requests, and a route is very spiky, the estimate will be useless.

amanda: Two ideas: (a) add a reservoir-style short-window high-priority sampling for quota-sensitive endpoints, (b) surface a confidence interval on the burn rate (e.g. low/med/high) when sampling is low.

sophie: Love (b) — lower cognitive load. For (a), ops teams will want a simple opt-in flag per route so we don't burn telemetry budget across all routes.

chris: Implementation sketch for SDK opt-in header (example Python):
```python
# optional client opt-in for quota-sensitive sampling
client = RWClient(...)
client.enable_quota_sensitive_sampling(route_id='billing-check')
# results in per-request header:
# X-RW-Quota-Sample: high
```

kelly: Console UX note: if we show time-to-soft-cap, also include 'what changed' hint (e.g., batching toggled, major spike). Small tipstrings + link to runbook.

tom: About breaking changes — Go SDK v1.9 will default `AutoBatch=false`? If we flip default we risk changing customers' burn rates overnight. We need a clear migration plan and a 'compat' header for the transitional period.

sophie: Do not flip defaults without an extended deprecation period and analytics. Let's add a telemetry flag to track `auto_batch` usage for two months before any default change.

raj: Sounds good. Action items: (1) backend: expose server-side token-counter API and support `X-RW-Client-Batch` and `X-RW-Quota-Sample` headers; (2) SDKs: add opt-in helper to emit those headers; (3) Console: show server vs attributed counts and confidence bands; (4) Eng: run two-week rollout with telemetry flag to measure `auto_batch` usage.

amanda: I'll draft the Console copy for the confidence bands + runbook link.

chris: I'll open an SDK PR for Python + Go to add the helper and the header emission behind opt-in. Will include tests that assert header correctness.

tom: I'll coordinate the telemetry flag and a dashboard to monitor `auto_batch` adoption.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: telemetry-flag-gate -> staging (ETA 23m). :rocket:

sophie: Thanks all — please add your PR links and I'll collate for a design review on Friday.
